Module io.github.brantunger.unruly.core
Package io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.language

Class MessageText

java.lang.Object
io.github.brantunger.unruly.api.language.MessageText
public final class MessageText extends Object
Shortens and escapes text a language didn't write, such as a fact name, an option value, an import or its library's own error text, for a message, as the engine does in its own messages. Such text can hold line breaks, bidi controls or lone surrogates, and a message the engine or a language logs mustn't let it start a log line of its own or hide part of the line. It delegates to the engine's own escaping rather than keeping a copy of it.

Use it for text the engine shows as it came: a message a language logs itself, the message of an exception its own library sees first, and the issues it throws in an InvalidExpressionException, which the engine copies untouched into the RuleCompilationException it reports. Use quote(java.lang.String) for a name and escape(truncate(text)) for other text. To end such text with a note of the language's own, such as " (caused by ...)", cut it with escapeWithin(String, int), escapeWithin(String, int, int) or quoteWithin(String, int), giving it the room the rest of the message leaves: the escaped result, its ... (N more characters) included, fits in that room, so the note stays whole.

The engine shortens to 1,000 characters and escapes the message of an InvalidExpressionException, the message of a warning's issue when it logs it, and the message of an exception from ExpressionCompiler.checkFactName(java.lang.String) when it logs it or, at load(), reports it for a declared fact. Leave a message the engine shortens raw: the engine escapes it itself, and the count of what was left out of escaped text counts escaped characters. Every cut the engine and this class make, but truncate(java.lang.String)'s, falls between code points and never inside an escape the engine writes or inside raw text that reads as one (a backslash and n, r or t, or a backslash, u and four lowercase hex digits): such text is left out whole, so up to 5 fewer characters show. A language may instead escape such a message itself, when the escaped message fits in 1,000 characters, as escapeWithin(text, MAX_TEXT_LENGTH) makes it; the engine then never shortens it.

The escapes, the note ... (N more characters) and the limits, MAX_NAME_LENGTH (200 characters, UTF-16 units) for a name and MAX_TEXT_LENGTH (1,000) for other text, are fixed for 2.x. javac inlines the two constants into the classes that read them. Which characters are escaped follows Unicode: format characters and space separators are read from the running JDK's Unicode version, so a later JDK may escape more characters as Unicode marks them, and a later 2.x release may escape more kinds of character.

  • Method Details

    • escape

      public static String escape(String text)
      Escapes text for a message, without shortening it. \n, \r and \t become those two-character escapes. Every other ISO control character, line or paragraph separator, space separator (category Zs) other than U+0020, format character (category Cf), other Default_Ignorable_Code_Point character and lone surrogate becomes a backslash, u and four lowercase hex digits, one for each UTF-16 unit, so an escaped character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane becomes two escapes, and each escaped unit shows as 2 or 6 characters. Everything else is kept, a valid surrogate pair such as an emoji included. A backslash isn't escaped, so escaping text twice gives the same text.

      Space separators and format characters are those of the running JDK's Unicode version (Character.getType(int)): the space separators are U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000 to U+200A, U+202F, U+205F and U+3000 besides U+0020. The other default-ignorable characters are U+034F, U+115F to U+1160, U+17B4 to U+17B5, U+180B to U+180F, U+2065, U+3164, U+FE00 to U+FE0F, U+FFA0, U+FFF0 to U+FFF8 and U+E0000 to U+E0FFF.

      To put long text in a message, shorten it first and escape it after, escape(truncate(text)), so a cut never falls inside an escape this writes. The result can be up to six times longer than the 1,000 characters kept, since a character escapes to at most 6, so use it only for text the engine won't shorten again. Leave a message the engine shortens raw: the engine escapes it itself (see the class description). To fit escaped text into a room, use escapeWithin(String, int).

      Parameters:
      text - The text
      Returns:
      The text, escaped
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if text is null

    • truncate

      public static String truncate(String text)
      Shortens text for a message to at most 1,000 characters (UTF-16 units), without escaping it. Text of at most 1,000 characters is returned as it is. Longer text keeps its first 1,000 characters, or 999 when the 1,000th is a high surrogate, so the text never ends in half a character, followed by ... (N more characters), where N counts the text's own characters left out. 1,000 is also the length above which the engine shortens the messages the class description lists, such as that of an InvalidExpressionException.

      Shorten first and escape after, escape(truncate(text)), so a cut never falls inside an escape and N counts the original text. Don't shorten text that is already escaped.

      Parameters:
      text - The text, not escaped
      Returns:
      The text, shortened if it was longer
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if text is null

    • quote

      public static String quote(String name)
      Shortens a name for a message to at most 200 characters (MAX_NAME_LENGTH, UTF-16 units), then escapes it. The cut falls between code points and before raw text that reads as an escape, which is left out whole, so up to 5 fewer characters show; ... (N more characters) follows, as truncate(java.lang.String) writes it, N counting the name's own characters left out. It adds no quotes: write them around it, as in "fact '" + MessageText.quote(name) + "'".
      Parameters:
      name - The name, such as a fact's, an option's or a class's
      Returns:
      The name, shortened if it was longer, then escaped
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if name is null

    • escapeWithin

      public static String escapeWithin(String text, int room)
      Escapes text for a message as escape(java.lang.String) does, shortened first if its escaped form is longer than room characters: to as many of its first characters as fit in room with ... (N more characters) after them, as truncate(java.lang.String) writes it. Use it to keep what a message says after the text, such as a closing note, whole: give it the room the rest of the message leaves.

      N counts the text's own characters left out, as given, not escaped ones. The cut falls between code points, so never inside a surrogate pair or an escape this writes, and never inside an escape the text already holds, or inside raw text that reads as one (\n, \r, \t, or a backslash, u and four lowercase hex digits): such text is left out whole. escape(java.lang.String) leaves an escape the text holds as it is, so a cut inside one would show it cut in half.

      The result is at most room characters, unless room is too small for the note alone: then the result is the note alone, and nothing is thrown. A negative room is taken as 0. Empty text is returned empty, whatever the room.

      Parameters:
      text - The text, raw, or with escapes the engine already wrote
      room - The most characters the escaped text may take, the note included
      Returns:
      The text, shortened if it didn't fit, then escaped
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if text is null

    • escapeWithin

      public static String escapeWithin(String text, int most, int room)
      Escapes text within a room as escapeWithin(String, int) does, showing at most its first most characters (UTF-16 units). Where most falls inside a surrogate pair or just after a lone high surrogate, or inside an escape the text holds or raw text that reads as one, that is left out whole, as quote(java.lang.String) leaves it out at 200, so up to 5 fewer characters show. A most of 0 or less shows none of a non-empty text, only the note. With a room of Integer.MAX_VALUE, the text is shortened to most characters alone.
      Parameters:
      text - The text, raw, or with escapes the engine already wrote
      most - The most of its characters to show
      room - The most characters the escaped text may take, the note included
      Returns:
      The text, shortened if it didn't fit or is longer than most, then escaped
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if text is null

    • quoteWithin

      public static String quoteWithin(String name, int room)
      Quotes a name for a message as quote(java.lang.String) does, or, if that is longer than room characters, escapes it within the room as escapeWithin(String, int) does. Either way it shows no more of the name than quote(java.lang.String) does. An empty name is quoted as empty, whatever the room. It adds no quotes.
      Parameters:
      name - The name, such as a fact's, an option's or a class's
      room - The most characters the quoted name may take, the note included
      Returns:
      The name, shortened if it was longer or didn't fit, then escaped
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if name is null
